name: Approval without vote
title: RECOMMENDATION FOR SECOND READING on the Council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the greenhouse gas emissions accounting of transport services
part_text:
The European Parliament has approved a new EU law on how the climate impact of transport services is counted. Companies that move goods or people will use one common method to calculate their greenhouse gas emissions, based on an existing international standard. The European Commission will build a free, simpler calculation tool for transport operators. Companies should use their own measured data where possible and fall back on estimates only when needed. The Commission will also look at whether to count emissions from making and disposing of vehicles and fuels in a future revision.

- What changes: one shared EU method for counting transport emissions, plus a free calculation tool from the Commission.
- Who it affects: transport operators moving goods or people, and their customers who want emissions figures.
- What happens next: the law is adopted; the tool is due within four years, and a review of wider emissions within four years after the rules start to apply.
